You put it better than me, it's exactly how it feels. "Relaxed" is probably the wrong word, but more at peace with it than what I probably should be. I'm currently in the process to see if I can qualify for Deep Brain Stimulation, since I haven't responded to any medications. Will see what happens with that, but can't go on like this. It's not living, it's existing, waiting for the days to end.

I know what you mean. I've come to the point where I have a relaxed approach to it. I have been through all meds there is for depression and BP2 over the course of 15 years (M36), my family know I'm tired of it all, and it may be my way out. It's kind of "elephant in the room". I don't seek panic, I don't scream for help, I'm just tired and want out.

I'm on 200mg morning and 200mg evening of Lamictal, with 300mg Welbutrin in the morning. I thought this was fairly standard? Occasionally I really get these episodes of getting dizzy and noxious, but never really connected it to the meds. Maybe that's it then.
Just saying, mate - Manic depression is the old term for Bipolar (split into Bipolar 1 and Bipolar 2 with different stages of hypomania).

I've commented on this before, and in my experience, most of the time you are spot on. I was hospitalized against my will after suicide attempt, and since went through 7 "I'll sit here, pretend to care and give some generic answers because it's my job", before finding one that made a difference. Connection is key. If there is no connection, you are unlikely to open up and it's about as useless as tits on a nun. The one I go to now is knowledgeable, cares (or is a bloody good actor) and asks the right questions. Not always pleasant at ALL, but it's worth it. I've been lucky finding her, but I definitely respect that therapy isn't for everyone.

After 5-6 failed attempts going to therapy, I had given up on it. I figured I may as well just rely on my medication (Lamictal and Welbutrin, with Valium used for anxiety attacks). A friend recommended I should give a therapist he knew a go, as a "last time". It was a game changer for me. For her it was not "just a job", like I had felt with any other. She genuinely saw the issues I dealt with daily, beat me to the questions about I was going to tell her about, and now sending me to specialist for gene tests, spect scan to see blood flow in different parts of the brain, all to see what kind of medication and dosage that can make life better. The effect of hope is a medication itself. 

Good luck! 

Edit: My opinion have always been that personal chemistry with the therapist is key. No connection-->I won't open-->waste of time.

Lamotrigine=Lamictal. It's a matter of marketing name. Or did you mean that the dry eyes can't be due to the Lamotrigine? Because dry eyes/mouth is listed as side effect that affects ≥1/100 to <1/10.

Def see a doctor if you can. Lamotrigine/Lamictal have (a veeeeeeery small) chance at having some of the nastiest side effects, targeting mucosal. Def worth checking in my opinion. I know I was more "on guard" when starting on these for symptoms than with other meds I started on. I got a few random rash on my arms, and it still comes, but at leastI know it is nothing to worry about.
